text.content: Initial boundary test: Mossa et al. (2025) treats architecture and ERP characteristics including integration as related characteristics; Odoo documents multitier architecture and modules; Frank (2004) studies architectural design for integration of distributed ERP/e-commerce systems. The evidence supports keeping Architecture and Integrations conceptually separate but related; no activation of an Integrations taxonomy node is justified yet.

text.content: ASR-7 edition/plan test completed with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central. Microsoft documents Essentials and Premium within the same product family. Essentials covers finance, sales, operations, purchasing/payables, inventory, supply planning, projects and warehouse management; Premium includes all Essentials capabilities plus Manufacturing and Service Management. Learn documentation also states that the company experience setting controls which functionality is enabled and that Essentials users cannot open Premium-configured companies. This establishes material Edition/Plan → Functional Scope divergence. It does not establish that the plans are different System Types; plan/licensing is context for evaluating the actual functional scope.
